payload.rebuttal: argued: This mutation changes only the pool's opening formula (dropping the lens-count multiplier on REVIEW_FLOOR_USD), which is criterion 2's claim ("floored at REVIEW_FLOOR_USD once per name in review.LENSES"), not criterion 1's. Criterion 1's claim is about the cut mechanism once the pool is already low, and its three cells are pinned by the spec's own notes to budget_usd=8.2, giving a remainder of exactly $8.00, the same value as REVIEW_FLOOR_USD times four lenses. At that exact figure max(8.0, 8.0) and max(8.0, 2.0) both equal 8.0, so no witness built on those prescribed numbers can tell the two formulas apart; the deviation only shows up when the floor term would otherwise dominate, which criterion 1's cells never let happen. The report's own failing-test list already names test_a_review_that_fits_its_pool_runs_every_session_capped_at_what_is_left (criterion 2's own witness) as failing under this exact edit, so the formula this mutation breaks is already guarded by the criterion whose claim covers it. I left criterion 1's cells at the figures the spec specified rather than bending them to catch a defect outside that criterion's own claim.
